API.name: Authentication bypass
API.description: An attacker bypasses authentication and impersonates a legitimate user.

API.name: Injection attack
API.description: Untrusted input changes a command or database query.

API.name: Broken authorization
API.description: A user accesses operations or records outside their permissions.

S3.name: Public bucket exposure
S3.description: Sensitive objects are publicly readable due to a policy or ACL.

S3.name: Unauthorized object modification
S3.description: An attacker modifies or replaces stored objects.

S3.name: Missing access logging
S3.description: Object access cannot be reliably traced during an investigation.

S3.name: Over-permissive bucket access
S3.description: A principal has broader object permissions than required.

EC2.name: Public SSH exposure
EC2.description: An internet-accessible SSH service is targeted with stolen credentials.

EC2.name: Unpatched operating system
EC2.description: Known vulnerabilities allow an attacker to gain elevated access.

EC2.name: Instance metadata credential theft
EC2.description: An attacker obtains temporary IAM credentials from instance metadata.

EC2.name: Resource exhaustion
EC2.description: Workload or attacker activity exhausts CPU, memory, or disk.

RDS.name: Public database exposure
RDS.description: The database is reachable from untrusted networks.

RDS.name: Weak database credentials
RDS.description: Weak or reused credentials allow unauthorized access.

RDS.name: Unencrypted data
RDS.description: Sensitive database data is exposed at rest or in transit.

RDS.name: Excessive database privileges
RDS.description: Application users have more database access than required.

ECS.name: Vulnerable container image
ECS.description: A known image vulnerability is exploited inside the workload.

ECS.name: Over-permissive task role
ECS.description: A compromised task can call unnecessary AWS APIs.

ECS.name: Exposed container port
ECS.description: A task is reachable directly instead of only through an approved entry point.
